question: What is the meaning of number of joints in relation to physical composition?
description: The number of joints in relation to physical composition refers to the count of connections or articulations between different parts of a structure or product. This information is crucial for understanding the mechanical integrity, flexibility, and overall performance of the physical object. In the context of sustainable construction, optimizing the number of joints can lead to improved durability, reduced maintenance, and enhanced recyclability. For instance, in the MPO (Material Property Ontology), the composition property facet includes information about constituent materials and their mass, which can be used to assess the physical properties and performance of a product. Similarly, in the Building Topology Ontology (BOT), the element class and its subelement class help to identify and manage the complex relationships between different building components, including joints. Therefore, the number of joints is an essential aspect of physical composition that can significantly impact the sustainability and performance of a product or building.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.
